title: 2 Rooks vs 2 Rooks
summary: Move the king out of its own rook’s way to create a ladder mate.

nodes.question: How can White make progress against the back-rank rooks?
nodes.explanation: Castling has already placed the white king on c1 and rook on d1. The rook on a7 confines Ke8, but White needs room for a second rook to attack from b1.

branches.title: Walk to a1, then swing the rook
commentary: Begin after castling and the illustrated ...Rf8. Earlier checking and material-winning examples are source context; castling itself is not tablebase-certified.
Kb1 starts clearing c1 and d1 while keeping the king on the back rank, where the black rooks cannot give a useful check.
Rfg8 waits on the back rank. Moving this rook away from that rank allows a checking skewer against the other rook.
Ka1 completes the retreat and clears b1 for White’s d-rook.
Rf8 returns along the back rank, preserving Black’s defensive arrangement for the selected source line.
Rb1 uses the space the king has just cleared and threatens Rb8 mate. The a7 rook keeps the king off the seventh rank.
Kd8 tries to move away, but remains in range of the b-file ladder check.
Rb8# is actual checkmate. The b8 rook checks along the eighth rank, and the a7 rook cuts off the seventh-rank escapes.

branches.title: Swing before the king has shelter
commentary: Compare the source’s rook activation before the king retreats to a1.
Rd6 gives up the win: it leaves the white king exposed to useful checks along the first rank.
Rh1+ uses the newly opened back rank to start checking the king.
Kb2 leaves the back rank to answer the check.
Rf2+ brings the other rook down with tempo. Black’s checking activity holds the exact position drawn.
Kc3 continues the illustrated escape. The tablebase confirms a draw, so this active-looking rook swing does not force a win.

exercises.prompt: Why does the king retreat to a1?
exercises.answer: It clears b1 for the rook without allowing the black rooks useful checks. Rb1 then threatens the ladder mate Rb8.

exercises.prompt: Why does immediate Rd6 fail to force a win?
exercises.answer: Moving that rook off the first rank lets ...Rh1+ expose the king. Black gains active checks instead of waiting helplessly on the eighth rank.

startContext: Begin at 77 seconds after the source’s queenside castling and ...Rf8. The six-piece post-castling position is visually reconstructed and checked exactly. The opening claim that White still has castling rights is a source stipulation, not an inference from a static board, and is outside the tablebase scope. Selected waiting moves and the premature rook swing are encoded.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
